reports.title: Iran Rejects U.S. Peace Terms as 'Surrender.' The Strait Stays Closed.
reports.subtitle: Tehran's counterproposal demands war reparations and full Hormuz sovereignty. Trump called it totally unacceptable. Drones are still flying.

reports.title: Trump Tells His Own Justices to Be 'Loyal.' The Court Hears It.
reports.subtitle: After SCOTUS killed his tariffs and is expected to kill his birthright citizenship order, Trump called out Gorsuch and Barrett by name.

reports.title: Trump Flies to Beijing Thinking He Has Leverage. China Disagrees.
reports.subtitle: China's rare earths card turned the October trade truce into a template Beijing plans to repeat. The May 14 summit will reveal who actually blinks.

reports.title: The Courts Have Now Killed Two Different Tariff Regimes. Trump Keeps Building New Ones.
reports.subtitle: The first $166B in IEEPA refunds arrive today. Last week a trade court struck down the 10% replacement tariff.

reports.title: The EU Is Forcing Google to Open Android to Rival AI. This Could Matter More Than Any AI Regulation.
reports.subtitle: Under the Digital Markets Act, the European Commission has drafted binding measures requiring Alphabet to let competing AI services run on Android.

reports.title: Germany Wants to Ban Social Media for Kids Under 14. The Age Verification Problem Will Break It.
reports.subtitle: The SPD's proposal uses the EU Digital Identity Wallet as the enforcement mechanism. That is either a serious policy or a data collection system with a safety branding.

reports.title: The Supreme Court Killed Section 2. Now Every State Is Redrawing Maps.
reports.subtitle: The 6-3 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais used manipulated DoJ data to gut the last protection in the Voting Rights Act. Louisiana already suspended live elections.

reports.title: The Mifepristone Stay Expires Today. SCOTUS Has Not Acted.
reports.subtitle: Justice Alito's one-week pause on the Fifth Circuit's mail-order abortion ban runs out May 11. If the court stays silent, two-thirds of American abortions stop being accessible by mail overnight.

reports.title: Cerebras Is Pricing Its IPO at $150 a Share. The Market Thinks It Will Open Worth $50 Billion.
reports.subtitle: 20x oversubscribed, backed by OpenAI and AWS, the AI chipmaker claims its wafer-scale processor beats Nvidia at inference. That claim is the entire bet.

reports.title: The Fed Is Stuck. Iran Is Why.
reports.subtitle: Oil at $104. Inflation at 3.3%. April CPI drops tomorrow. PIMCO warns that the war in Iran has made the Fed's next move a trap with no clean exit.

reports.title: Trump Sanctioned China's Oil Supply Chain to Gain Leverage Before the Summit. China Already Priced It In.
reports.subtitle: Washington's April 24 sanctions targeting Hengli Petrochemical and 40 shipping entities were supposed to be summit leverage. A CounterPunch analysis argues they were actually America's last chip, spent.

reports.title: China's AI Chips Achieved Day Zero Parity with Nvidia. Jensen Huang Says His China Share Is Now Zero.
reports.subtitle: When DeepSeek V4 launched, Huawei, Cambricon and Moore Threads ran it the same day. That ended Nvidia's real advantage in China: timing.

reports.title: The EU Just Rewrote Its AI Law Before It Took Effect. OpenAI Is Cooperating. Anthropic Is Not.
reports.subtitle: The Digital Omnibus deal pushed high-risk AI compliance to 2027 at 4:30am after talks collapsed twice. OpenAI is offering EU regulators model access. Anthropic is holding off.

reports.title: Trump Made the Post Office a Gatekeeper for Who Can Vote by Mail. USPS Is Losing $2 Billion a Quarter.
reports.subtitle: The March 31 executive order gives USPS the power to flag or reject mail ballots tied to people not on DHS-curated voter rolls. Courts are watching. So is USPS's board, which needs Trump's help to stay solvent.

reports.title: Putin Proposed His Friend Schroeder as Ukraine Mediator. Every Party That Matters Rejected Him Within 24 Hours.
reports.subtitle: Germany, Ukraine, and the EU all said no. That is not the interesting part. The interesting part is why Putin floated a name he knew would be refused.

reports.title: China's Factory Prices Just Hit a 45-Month High. The Iran War Did It, and Beijing Cannot Undo It.
reports.subtitle: China's PPI jumped 2.8% in April, ending 41 months of factory deflation. Cost-push inflation from Iranian oil disruptions is pressuring manufacturer margins in an economy where domestic demand is still weak.

reports.title: Samsung Faces Its First Strike in 88 Years. Google, Apple, and Qualcomm Are Worried.
reports.subtitle: A 18-day planned walkout over performance bonuses could squeeze the memory supply chain at the worst possible moment for global AI hardware demand.
